category_title: Students with mild intellectual disability capable of logical leadership roles
minimal_context: Ben is sitting at a computer in the classroom to review his homework on Google Drive and set new learning goals.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Ben, it is time for self-evaluation. Please open your homework on Google Drive so we can set new goals and find out what you have to improve.

STUDENT: I don't want to look at the Drive. I don't want to do this right now.

TUTOR: What do you think you should pay more attention to for the next steps of your learning tasks?

STUDENT: Study. Good.

TUTOR: Can you write down a full sentence about your suggestions for your new goals?

STUDENT: (Sighs, looking frustrated) No. Just... read. Better.

options.A: Ask the student to set up a goal after finishing the evaluation of the homework; if that is not enough, provide help by asking him to think of one more thing to improve.
options.B: Use Quiet Time as a supportive strategy to prevent an emotional overload, entailing the student avoiding or withdrawing from the classroom environment for a time-limited period during the session.
options.C: Terminate the task demands and remove the homework and Google Drive materials from the student for 10 seconds during the self-evaluation session.
options.D: Simplify the instructions provided to the student for the self-evaluation task and the Google Drive homework review during this session.
